# Vienna 1683 – Institutions, law & governance

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from eras/europe-1683-vienna.yaml — do not edit -->

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Written, published law code** [`written_law_code`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/written_law_code.md) — K4, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Criminal law is codified in the Ferdinandea (1656). Civil law is custom, Roman law and separate ordinances; drafts of a Lower Austrian Landrecht were never enacted. Local: Constitutio Criminalis Ferdinandea; Tractatus de juribus incorporalibus (1679); police ordinances.
- **Rule of law and separation of powers** [`rule_of_law`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/rule_of_law.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. The emperor respects the estates' privileges in practice, but he is the source of law and can dispense from it. In the siege Starhemberg rules by martial law. Elsewhere: England: Parliament against Stuart prerogative; Dutch Republic.
- **Independent judges and judicial review** [`independent_judiciary_judicial_review`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/independent_judiciary_judicial_review.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Courts are the ruler's: city court, Lower Austrian government, Reichshofrat. Judges are removable and appeals end with the emperor. Local: Reichshofrat (imperial aulic council, sits in Vienna); Stadt- und Landgericht.
- **Habeas corpus and fair trial** [`habeas_corpus_fair_trial`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/habeas_corpus_fair_trial.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Trials are inquisitorial, secret and written; the accused has little defence and confession may be forced. Nobles and university members have their own courts. Elsewhere: England: Habeas Corpus Act (1679), jury trial.
- **Representative government (elected assembly)** [`representative_government`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/representative_government.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept low. The Lower Austrian estates (prelates, lords, knights, towns) meet in the Landhaus and vote the taxes the court demands; their real power was broken after 1620. Peasants are not represented. Local: Landhaus in the Herrengasse; the estates' Landmarschall and Verordnete; Vienna's inner and outer council. Elsewhere: England: Parliament; Poland: Sejm; Regensburg: permanent Reichstag since 1663.
- **Selection of officials by lot (sortition)** [`sortition`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sortition.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Known from Venice and from ancient authors. Office here follows birth, co-option and the ruler's confirmation. Elsewhere: Venice: lot and ballot in electing the doge.
- **Direct democracy (citizen assembly voting on laws)** [`citizen_assembly`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/citizen_assembly.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept low. Known from Athens in school texts and from Swiss Landsgemeinden. In Vienna it would be called sedition. Elsewhere: Swiss rural cantons.
- **Secret ballot** [`secret_ballot`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/secret_ballot.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Monasteries elect abbots and the university its officers by written or secret vote under canon and statute law. City offices are filled under the government's supervision. Local: Schottenstift and other chapters; university nations and faculties.
- **Peaceful transfer of power and loyal opposition** [`peaceful_transfer_of_power`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/peaceful_transfer_of_power.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Succession is hereditary in the lands and elective in the Empire (Leopold was elected in 1658) and in Poland. Opposition to the ruler is treason.
- **Written constitution** [`written_constitution`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/written_constitution.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. The Empire has fundamental laws (Golden Bull, electoral capitulations, Westphalia); Bohemia has the Renewed Land Ordinance of 1627. Each land holds its own privileges.
- **Federalism and subsidiarity** [`federalism_subsidiarity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/federalism_subsidiarity.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The monarchy is a union of lands under one ruler, each with its estates and law. The Empire is a federation of princes; its Circles send troops to relieve Vienna. Elsewhere: Swiss Confederation; United Provinces.
- **Treaties, diplomacy and international law** [`international_law_sovereignty`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/international_law_sovereignty.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Resident ambassadors, treaties and Grotius are standard. The Peace of Vasvár (1664) with the Porte runs twenty years; Caprara's embassy to renew it failed in 1682. Local: papal nuncio Francesco Buonvisi; Reichshofkanzlei and Hofkanzlei; Georg Christoph von Kunitz, imperial resident, carried along in the Ottoman camp.
- **Secure property rights and land registry** [`property_rights_land_registry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/property_rights_land_registry.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. City houses and their burdens are entered in land books kept since the 14th century. Noble estates are listed for tax in the estates' Gültbuch. Peasants hold land from lords. Local: Vienna Grundbuch; Lower Austrian Gültbuch (Landhaus).
- **Contracts, notaries and merchant courts** [`commercial_law_contract_enforcement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/commercial_law_contract_enforcement.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Contracts and bills are enforced by city and government courts, slowly. No merchant court or bill-of-exchange code exists; privileged wholesalers have their own status. Local: Niederlagsverwandte; public notaries. Elsewhere: Leipzig, Frankfurt, Bolzano: fair courts and exchange ordinances.
- **Patent law** [`patents`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/patents.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The emperor grants individual privileges for books, manufactures and inventions as favours, often to courtiers. No general rule rewards the first inventor. Elsewhere: Venice (1474); England: Statute of Monopolies (1624).
- **Copyright for authors** [`copyright`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copyright.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Imperial printing privileges protect the printer for some years, not the author. Reprinting across borders is normal.
- **Standard weights and measures** [`standard_weights_measures`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standard_weights_measures.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Vienna has its own ell, fathom (Klafter), Metzen and Eimer, checked by the city; two iron ells hang at St Stephen's. Every land and many towns differ. Local: iron ells at St Stephen's main door; city weighing house.
- **Census and registration of births and deaths** [`census_vital_registration`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/census_vital_registration.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Parishes keep baptism, marriage and burial books. City coroners record every death with a cause (Totenbeschauprotokolle, kept since 1648). Nobody has counted the living. Local: Totenbeschauprotokolle; parish registers of St Stephen's, St Michael's, the Schotten. Elsewhere: London: Bills of Mortality, analysed by Graunt (1662).
- **Public accounts, audit and budget** [`public_accounts_audit`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_accounts_audit.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept low. The Hofkammer has a court audit office but no budget and no overview of debts. Its president Sinzendorf was convicted of embezzlement in 1680. The estates audit their own treasury. Local: Hofkammer and Hofbuchhalterei; estates' treasury in the Landhaus.
- **Merit-based civil service (examinations)** [`merit_civil_service`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/merit_civil_service.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Offices go by birth, patronage, purchase of expectancies and conversion; a law degree helps. Jesuits report China's examinations.
- **Universal elementary schooling** [`universal_schooling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_schooling.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Parish and German schools teach reading, catechism and sums for a fee; the Jesuits run free Latin schools for boys. Nothing is compulsory. Country children mostly get none. Local: Jesuit grammar schools; city school at St Stephen's; Ursuline convent school for girls (nuns in Vienna since 1660, school house from 1666). Elsewhere: Gotha: compulsory schooling under the Schulmethodus (1642).
- **University (self-governing body of teachers and students)** [`university`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/university.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Founded 1365. Since 1623 philosophy and theology belong to the Jesuits and the university is joined to their college. Law and medicine are secular. Students form armed companies. Local: University of Vienna and Jesuit college (Universitätsviertel); Paul de Sorbait, professor of medicine, rector 1668. Elsewhere: Leiden, Padua, Altdorf, Jena: newer science and medicine.
- **Scientific society or academy** [`scientific_academy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_academy.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium. None in Vienna. The emperor is patron of the physicians' Academia Naturae Curiosorum, which has no seat. Founding one needs court favour and must not offend the Jesuits. Local: Wilhelm von Schröder FRS; Leopold I, a learned patron and composer. Elsewhere: London: Royal Society; Paris: Académie des sciences; Hanover: Leibniz, who later lobbies for a Vienna academy.
- **Organised industrial research laboratory** [`industrial_research_lab`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/industrial_research_lab.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept medium. The Kunst- und Werkhaus on the Tabor (1676) had a chemical laboratory and workshops for majolica, silk and wool. It lies outside the walls and burns in 1683. Local: Kunst- und Werkhaus am Tabor; court apothecary and court alchemists.
- **Public library and museum** [`public_library_museum`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_library_museum.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The court library admits scholars by favour; the imperial treasury and art chamber are shown to visitors of rank. Nothing is open to the public. Local: Hofbibliothek; imperial Schatzkammer and Kunstkammer in the Hofburg. Elsewhere: Oxford: Ashmolean Museum opens in 1683; Milan: Ambrosiana; Oxford: Bodleian.
- **Freedom of the press** [`free_press`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/free_press.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Pre-censorship lies with the university (in effect the Jesuits) and the bishop; printers hold revocable privileges. Uncensored print is smuggled from the Reich cities and Holland. Elsewhere: Dutch Republic; England (licensing lapses 1679–1685 and ends 1695).
- **Abolition of slavery** [`abolition_of_slavery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abolition_of_slavery.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. On the Turkish frontier both sides enslave and ransom captives. In 1683 Tatar raiders carry off tens of thousands from Lower Austria. Peasants are hereditary subjects owing Robot. Local: Trinitarians (ransoming of captives; in Vienna only from 1689); Leopold's Robot patent for Bohemia (1680).
- **Women's legal rights and suffrage** [`women_rights_suffrage`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/women_rights_suffrage.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Wives are under their husband's guardianship. Widows may continue a workshop or printing house, noblewomen manage estates, and convents give some women learning.
- **Perpetual endowment (waqf, foundation, trust)** [`charitable_endowment_waqf`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/charitable_endowment_waqf.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Monasteries, the Bürgerspital, masses, student stipends and dowry funds live from perpetual endowments. Much land is in the dead hand of the Church. Local: Bürgerspital; Schottenstift; Hofspital; student bursaries of the university.
- **Craft guilds and apprenticeship** [`guilds_apprenticeship`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/guilds_apprenticeship.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Guilds control mastership and numbers. Court-exempt craftsmen (Hofbefreite) and unlicensed workers (Störer) compete with them. Guild members serve in the citizen companies on the walls. Local: Vienna craft guilds; Hofbefreite craftsmen; privileged wholesalers (Niederleger).
- **Permanent public health authority** [`public_health_board`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_health_board.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The plague of 1679 was denied for months. Plague ordinances, a magister sanitatis, pest house and coroners exist; action starts only when an epidemic is declared. Local: Paul de Sorbait (plague inquisitor 1679, Pest-Ordnung); medical faculty; Lazarett pest house (outside the walls). Elsewhere: Venice, Milan, Florence: permanent health magistracies.
- **Fire brigade, civil police and building rules** [`fire_brigade_police_building_codes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fire_brigade_police_building_codes.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Fire ordinances oblige householders and guilds to bring buckets, ladders and hooks; tower watchmen give the alarm. The Stadtguardia keeps the gates and the Rumorwache (1646) the streets. Local: Stadtguardia (main guard on Petersplatz); Rumorwache; watchman on St Stephen's tower; Unterkammeramt (city works office). Elsewhere: Amsterdam: Jan van der Heyden's fire hoses (1672).
- **Social insurance and poor relief** [`social_insurance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/social_insurance.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Help comes from the Bürgerspital, confraternities, guild chests and alms; begging is licensed. During the siege Bishop Kollonitsch organises care for the wounded, refugees and orphans. Local: Bürgerspital; Bishop Leopold Karl von Kollonitsch; guild and confraternity chests.
- **Trade unions and collective bargaining** [`trade_unions_collective_bargaining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/trade_unions_collective_bargaining.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Journeymen have brotherhoods with hostels and sick chests, and use boycotts and walk-outs. Authorities treat these as conspiracy and punish them. Local: journeymen's hostels (Herbergen).
